why: The biggest lever: Sonnet-class costs a fraction of Opus-class per token, and it is the documented recommended default for coding.
Adaptive-reasoning models default to high or xhigh effort; medium trims thinking-token spend at modest quality cost, and /effort still raises it for one session.
Subagent fan-out is where one prompt becomes many sessions; Haiku-class input is about a third of Sonnet's price.
Dynamic workflows default to unrestricted agent counts; small advises Claude to write leaner ones.
By default the literal word ultracode in a prompt launches a multi-agent workflow; off means workflows run only when asked for deliberately.
Fast mode bills roughly double per token; per-session opt-in stops it persisting silently across sessions.
The return-to-terminal recap is model-generated on your key.
Terminal titles are Haiku-generated per session; a small but pure saving.
